name: Jake Dearden
who: 247 Gym head coach and Red Bull athlete; Men's Doubles World Champion 2024, Elite 15 regular with a 49:07 PB at EMEA London 2026.
why: Follow him for polished high-performance training content and race breakdowns from someone who still races Elite 15 himself.
takeaway: Keep racing yourself even after you start coaching — it keeps your advice honest.

name: Rich Ryan
who: Founder of Reinforced Running; Elite 15 racer who ran 53:57 in Phoenix and is heading to the Stockholm World Championships.
why: His breakdowns of running strategy inside a Hyrox race are some of the most concretely useful coaching content in the sport.
takeaway: Work on your running strategy inside the race itself, not just station strength.

name: Robert James
who: Official Hyrox Ambassador and coach behind the Sub-60 program, built on science-backed pacing plans.
why: Go to him for a structured, data-driven path to breaking sub-60, not just motivation.
takeaway: Follow a structured, science-backed pacing plan toward a specific time goal instead of guessing splits.

name: Lukas Storath
who: The first Hyrox World Champion; now CEO and founder of Athletic Camps, running online Hyrox coaching.
why: One of the few voices who can talk about the sport's early days and its current programming with equal authority.
takeaway: Study the sport's early history to understand why current training methods evolved this way.

name: Quentin Pingliez
who: French coach who says he took the Mixed World and EU overall title in 2025; posts as @coach_pgz.
why: A rising French voice mixing his own recent results with day-to-day coaching content.
takeaway: Share your own current race results alongside your coaching content so advice stays grounded.

name: Tiago Lousa
who: Portuguese Hyrox coach with 58 races and 55 podiums logged; runs coaching under TheLousaWay.
why: Few coaches have that much race volume to draw lessons from, and he shares it openly.
takeaway: Rack up race volume deliberately — dozens of starts teach patterns a few races never will.

name: Jade Skillen
who: Hyrox performance coach sponsored by Puma and Mira Fit, the most-followed Hyrox coach on this list.
why: Consistent, brand-backed training content aimed at everyday racers, not just the elite field.
takeaway: Follow programming aimed at everyday racers, not just the elite field, if that's your level.

name: Greg Williams
who: Hyrox livestream co-commentator and host of Rox Lyfe, the weekly Hyrox podcast interviewing top athletes and coaches.
why: The closest thing the sport has to a reference show — deep athlete interviews every week.
reach: IG count not found; weekly podcast across Spotify/Apple/Amazon (approx 2026)
takeaway: Listen to in-depth athlete interviews weekly to learn training philosophy straight from top performers.

name: Till Schenk
who: Hyrox livestream co-commentator and Global Event Emcee/TV host for Hyrox and Eurosport, based in Munich; former 14-season Ironman athlete.
why: His race-day commentary is the voice most fans associate with the sport's biggest broadcasts.
takeaway: Bring endurance-sport background into how you pace and think through the longer stations.

name: Nick Bare
who: Fitness YouTuber (1.46M subscribers) whose cinematic, multi-part 'Hyrox Prep' series documented his own build toward the sport.
why: Brings a massive outside fitness/military audience into Hyrox with genuinely watchable long-form content.
takeaway: Document your full training build toward a race goal — filming your own prep builds accountability.

name: Amotti
who: Physical: 100 Season 2 winner and Team Korea member who took 2nd in the Doubles race at AIA Hyrox Singapore 2025.
why: Pulls a huge Netflix-built audience into Hyrox through upbeat training vlogs.
reach: IG follower count not independently confirmed; Physical: 100-driven following (approx 2026)
takeaway: Keep your training content upbeat and consistent — energy in your posts pulls in new racers.

name: Choi Seung-yeon
who: 4x CrossFit Games athlete and Physical: Asia star who took 2nd in Doubles at Hyrox Singapore 2025 alongside Amotti.
why: Elite CrossFit credibility plus mainstream Netflix fame makes her a strong entry point for new fans.
takeaway: Bring elite conditioning from another sport directly into Hyrox doubles rather than starting from scratch.

name: Meg Martin
who: Australian coach and founder of apparel brand M3GA; Hyrox Mixed Doubles age-group World Champion with a Women's Doubles APAC record.
why: Runs her own run clubs and coaching on top of racing, with a strong builder-not-just-athlete story.
takeaway: Commit to one fixed doubles partner and drill pacing together toward a target time.

name: George Edwards
who: Hyrox coach and athlete linked to The Hybrid Project, posting as @ge_training.
why: A smaller-following coach worth a follow for straightforward, no-frills Hyrox programming.
takeaway: Keep your programming simple and no-frills rather than overcomplicating training with unnecessary variety.

name: Delphin Kruithof Kremer
who: Hyrox ambassador, athlete, and head coach offering triathlon, running, and Hyrox programming.
why: Worth following for programming that bridges endurance racing and Hyrox-specific training.
takeaway: Bridge endurance-sport training, like triathlon or running, with Hyrox-specific work instead of treating them separately.

name: Renaud Boutillier
who: French Hyrox coach posting training content as @renaud.hyrox.coach.
why: A smaller French-language voice for athletes who want coaching content outside English-language channels.
takeaway: Create training content in your own language if it reaches racers other channels miss.
